clue.text: Back in a tick

blocks.note: first meaning: to support a proposal or candidate
a very short moment of time

explanation.surface: Someone promising to return very shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in a tick' reads as one phrase, but it splits into a verb and a noun; 'in' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it, and a moment of time lasting one sixtieth of a minute is a tick.

clue.text: Composed a piece that's singled out

blocks.note: to set words to music is to compose
a + part, a piece of something

explanation.surface: A composer has written a work that has drawn special praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set apart has been distinguished or reserved from the rest, which is what singled out means.

clue.text: Choose at random from actors on a great deal

blocks.note: the actors in a play form its cast
lots means a large amount

explanation.surface: Picking performers haphazardly while they earn huge fees.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed after, so the second piece follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting lots means drawing marked tokens to settle a decision by chance, so it is choosing at random.

clue.text: Turned up college memorandum

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it so its bottom reads first

blocks.note: Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: A memo from a college has surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor, a crossword favourite for 'college'.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a short written message or reminder, which is what a memorandum is.

clue.text: Throw away food in error

blocks.note: chuck is old slang for food or grub
out means mistaken, as in 'your figures are out'

explanation.surface: Binning food by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck for food is dated British slang (also a cut of beef).
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck out is the informal phrasal verb for discarding something as rubbish.

clue.text: One a QC regrets calling?

blocks.note: surface reading: somebody a senior lawyer wishes they had never phoned
setter's reading: calling means summoning to give evidence in court, where the person turns against the side that called them

explanation.walkthrough: A QC (Queen's Counsel) is a senior British barrister; calling here is the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a court may declare a witness adverse when their testimony harms the party that summoned them, to that lawyer's dismay.

clue.text: Good in parts, Grace, guest at sea?

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A guest named Grace on a cruise is only partly a success.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from a Punch cartoon in which a curate, served a bad egg by his bishop, says parts of it are excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate's egg is the idiom for something with a mixture of good and bad qualities.

clue.text: Like a stale pork-pie past its sell-by date?

blocks.note: first meaning: tired and no longer fresh or original
second meaning, cryptically: a pork-pie is a style of flat-crowned headwear, here an aged one

explanation.surface: A meat pie left on the shelf too long.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork-pie hat is a round, flat-topped hat; the pie on the surface is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is the idiom for something outdated or tired, and a worn-out pork-pie is literally an aged piece of headgear.

clue.text: Sailor goes on to achieve objective

blocks.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
to get something is to achieve or obtain it

explanation.surface: A seaman persists in order to reach his goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is the aim one works towards, a synonym of objective as a noun.

clue.text: An unduly demanding activity a trainee soldier may have come across?

definitions.text: An unduly demanding activity a trainee soldier may have come across?

blocks.note: surface reading: any task that is far harder than it should be

blocks.clueFragment: a trainee soldier may have come across
blocks.note: setter's reading: a recruit literally crosses an army training circuit of walls, nets and ditches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come across' looks like 'encountered', but the recruit literally goes across it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used figuratively for a process full of hindrances, and literally for a military assault-training circuit.

clue.text: Tries to secure hose for laboratory equipment

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: tries out means tests
a hose is a flexible pipe

explanation.surface: Attempting to fasten a garden hose to lab apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Test tubes are small glass cylinders used in chemistry labs, so they are items of scientific apparatus.

clue.text: Electronic system in Rolls Royce broken by girl

indicators.note: something broken by another is split open with that other wedged inside

blocks.note: RR is the familiar abbreviation of the car maker
a girl's name, as crosswords often use

explanation.surface: A girl has damaged the electronics in a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a detection technology using radio waves to locate objects, an electronic system.

clue.text: Dim porter chasing piece of paper

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its opening letter
chasing means following behind, so one part comes after the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of paper
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A slow-witted hotel porter running after a scrap of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like it describes the porter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale and dim both describe light or colour that is weak and lacking brightness.

clue.text: Form of entertainment illustrated in woven tapestries

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into new patterns, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tapestry depicts some kind of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a cabaret act of undressing slowly to music, a type of entertainment.

clue.text: Fall out having row during holidays

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it

blocks.note: short holidays are breaks
a rank is a row or line, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: Falling out with someone after an argument on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall out' and 'row' both suggest a quarrel, but 'Fall out' is the military order to leave formation, and 'row' is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To break ranks is to leave a formation of soldiers, as the drill command to fall out instructs.

clue.text: Part of cricket pitch - report officially on end holding drop of rainwater

indicators.note: a single drop of a word is just its initial letter
holding something means keeping it inside, so one part wraps the other

blocks.note: to return a verdict or result is to report it formally
to cease is to end
the opening letter of rainwater

explanation.surface: An umpire formally reporting that rain stopped play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report officially' is the sense used for returning a verdict or election result; the rain and the stopping are just surface colour for cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The return crease is one of the white lines marked at each end of a cricket pitch, beside the stumps.

clue.text: Genuine bishop working with a chess federation

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a machine that is working is on
taken as written
FIDE is the world chess federation

explanation.surface: A real bishop on the board cooperating with chess's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for 'in good faith' and is used to mean authentic or real.

clue.text: Quit role in middle of act

indicators.note: placing something in the middle of a word puts it inside

blocks.note: a deed is an act
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor walked out of a part halfway through the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'role' and 'act' suggest theatre, but 'act' here is a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of depart, meaning left, which matches quit used as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Pool bar

blocks.note: first meaning: a pond where animals come to drink
second meaning: a pub, in jocular use

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool bar' reads like a bar by a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: In the wild it is a water source animals gather at; humorously it is a pub where people gather for drinks.

clue.text: One it upset - drop of cream, sour

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over so the word reads bottom to top
a mere drop of a word is just its initial letter

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards
taken as written
the opening letter of cream

explanation.surface: Someone was upset when a drop of cream turned sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic relates to vinegar or acetic acid, so it describes a sharp, vinegary sour taste.

clue.text: Exaggerate concerning party

blocks.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone making too much fuss about a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it to excess, the same as overstating or exaggerating it.

clue.text: Fielder with cap on head

blocks.note: a cap is a lid or covering
a head or headland is a point of land

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder wearing a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a fielding position in cricket on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder standing in that cricket position is called cover point, so the position names the player.

clue.text: Restrain army's leader, slightly mad

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: to gag someone is to restrain their speech
the opening letter of army

explanation.surface: Holding back an eccentric general.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for senile or a little crazy, which fits slightly mad.

clue.text: Irish one in country

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: An Irish person living somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Go round one Italian city

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it on all sides

blocks.note: a go or turn in a game
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An invitation to tour an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' reads like a phrasal verb, but 'Go' is a noun (a turn) and 'round' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the capital of Piedmont in northern Italy, a major Italian city.

clue.text: Self-control shown by others surrounding coach

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: the rest means the others
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Other people staying calm around a sports coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint means holding back one's impulses, which is the quality of self-control.

clue.text: Chinese-style dish, served in pouches, cooked with hint of yoghurt

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed up
a hint of a word is just its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of yoghurt

explanation.surface: A Chinese takeaway dish presented in little parcels with a yoghurt dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop suey is a stir-fried meat and vegetable dish invented in Chinese-American cooking.

clue.text: Mean to get home ahead of nurse

indicators.note: ahead of means placed in front, so one part comes first

blocks.note: being in means being at home
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Planning to go home before the nurse arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to have a purpose or plan, which is what the verb mean expresses in 'I mean to go'.
